title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"

target_networks.name: small CNNs (Model 1, Model 2, Random) on five image datasets

headline_result.text: Opus 5.5 reading ~125k CNN weights as text did accurate local arithmetic (e.g. CIFAR-10 vehicle/animal split) but named familiar datasets for unfamiliar ones and got all nine class pairs wrong on a label-permuted CIFAR-10 network.
headline_result.quote: Permuting CIFAR-10’s labels preserves the output split at the new indices, but every class pair the model interprets is then wrong, indicating reliance on remembered label order.

key_claims.claim: The model performs accurate local arithmetic, e.g. inferring about three optimizer steps from batch-norm statistics and finding the CIFAR-10 vehicle/animal output split.
key_claims.quote: batch-normalization statistics lead it to infer about three optimizer steps on networks stopped after three updates, and output-layer sign patterns recover the vehicle/animal split of CIFAR-10.

key_claims.claim: Semantic judgments fall back on familiar datasets: KMNIST read as MNIST, fast-food networks as CIFAR-10, a 99.57%-accurate SAT-6 network as CIFAR-10 animal photos.
key_claims.quote: the model names CIFAR-10 for CIFAR-10 networks but also for all three fast-food networks, relabels KMNIST as MNIST, reads a 99.57%-accurate SAT-6 network as CIFAR-10 animal photos

key_claims.claim: On a shuffled-weight control confidence fell to 45% but the model did not notice the scrambling.
key_claims.quote: On the shuffled control, confidence fell to 45%.

key_claims.claim: Sessions report reading first and last layers closely and sampling the middle; several partial-tracing claims failed verification, though no forward-pass test was run.
key_claims.quote: Across these reports, the model reads the edges closely and samples the middle sparsely (Figure 6).

key_claims.claim: The author argues edits that improve a benchmark should be shown to depend on claimed understanding rather than search over weights.
key_claims.quote: An editing result can be real even if the reading account is prior-driven, but an edit that improves a benchmark should be shown to depend on the claimed understanding rather than on search over weights.

limitations_stated.text: Only Claude Opus 5.5 at one effort level; most configurations run once on one seed with no significance tests.
limitations_stated.quote: Most configurations were run once, on a single random seed. The counts in the tables are descriptive; we report no confidence intervals or significance tests for the model’s answers

limitations_stated.text: Without tools, tracing 125k weights by hand may be infeasible; evidence on tracing is behavioral and partly self-reported.
limitations_stated.quote: Sessions had no calculator or code, and following about 125,000 weights by hand within one reply may be infeasible for any reader.

limitations_stated.text: Scoring was done through Claude Code without an independent second rater.
limitations_stated.quote: Scores were assigned without an independent second rater, so we cannot report inter-rater reli- ability.

notes_for_review: A single-author audit of the reading side of WSP with Claude Opus 5.5 (not Astra), using label permutation, shuffled weights, varied architectures and datasets of differing familiarity. The label-permutation control is a useful design, but it was run once, most conditions are single runs, scoring was done by Claude Code without a second rater, and materials are only available on request. Weight editing was not tested, and the author states the work does not refute Takehi et al.
